# Refund eligibility

Customers may request a refund within 14 calendar days of delivery when they provide an order number and proof of purchase. The request window concerns eligibility to ask for a refund; it is different from the time required for money to return after approval. Northstar Market reviews requests against product condition, the return reason, and any applicable consumer-protection requirement.

## Refund processing

After a refund is approved, funds return to the original payment method within 5 business days. A bank or card issuer may show the credit later than Northstar Market's processing window. Refund processing starts after approval, not when a customer first contacts support. Support must not promise an exact bank posting date because external payment providers control that final step.

## Returns and non-returnable items

Unused standard merchandise may be returned with its original packaging when the approved return instructions are followed. Personal-care products with broken seals, digital gift cards, and final-sale clearance items are not eligible for a change-of-mind refund. A defective item can still be reviewed under the defect process even if its packaging has been opened. A return shipment does not itself prove that a refund has been approved.

## Partial orders and delivery charges

For a partially fulfilled order, Northstar Market refunds only the affected items unless the entire order cannot reasonably be used. Original express-delivery charges are not refunded merely because a customer changes their mind. If Northstar Market confirms a fulfilment error, support may refund the relevant delivery charge as part of the approved remedy. Every exception must be recorded against the original order number.

## Evidence needed for a request

A customer should provide the original order number and proof of purchase when making a request. Support should identify the delivery date, product type, return reason, and order status before confirming whether the request fits the stated window. The presence of a parcel-tracking event, a customer email, or a return shipment is not equivalent to an approved refund. Approval remains a separate decision after the request is reviewed. This distinction is especially important for questions that mix eligibility timing with the later money-return timing.

## What this policy does not decide

This policy does not set stock levels, dispatch dates, card authorization rules, or a carrier's delivery estimate. It also cannot decide a supplier allocation or a promotion code's validity. A customer may qualify to request a refund and still need a separate operational review. If no clause above supports an exception, the correct answer is to say that the policy does not establish it, rather than creating an uncited promise. Only the approved document text is evidence for these rules.
